messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up: we need to settle on a canonical in-memory layout for multi-head tensors to optimize attention kernels. Options: head-major (B,H,S,Dh) vs seq-major (B,S,H,Dh) vs concat qkv in channels. Thoughts?
priya: My intuition: head-major (B,H,S,Dh) helps kernels that iterate per-head, but it makes KV cache indexing messy when KV cache is seq-major.
sam: Agreed. Also packing QKV as contiguous 3*Dh in the channel dim (B,S,3*H*Dh) lets us do a single GEMM for q,k,v, but we pay on the split cost afterwards.
maria: Want to call out that tensor cores / Triton kernels prefer 16/32-byte alignment per row. So whatever layout we pick we should mandate padded strides to 32 for cuBLAS compatibility. Small sequences are very sensitive to the extra copy.
alex: example layouts I keep thinking about:
```
# head-major (planar heads)
Q shape: [B, H, S, Dh]
# seq-major (NHWC-like)
Q shape: [B, S, H, Dh]
# contiguous qkv per token
QKV shape: [B, S, 3, H, Dh] OR flattened [B, S, 3*H*Dh]
```
priya: If we expose kernels that accept arbitrary strides, we avoid materializing copies. But strided access kills throughput unless kernels are implemented with gather-friendly code paths. That adds complexity to kernel selector.
sam: Right — tradeoff is: 1) Make kernel that assumes contiguous head slices => fastest, cheapest kernels but force a pre-format copy when layout mismatches. 2) Make universal strided kernel => slower but avoids copies.
infra-bot: perf-ci: perf regression detected: fused_qkv_nhwc kernel + pad32 stride mismatch -> 8% slower on A100 for seq_len=64.
maria: That matches microbenchmarks: fused fwd kernels rely on contiguous fast inner loops. A copy into NHWC contiguous buffer then run fused kernel is still often faster overall (memcpy+fast kernel vs slow kernel).
devon: For inference with KV cache we often append tokens incrementally. Sequence-major layout (B,S,H,Dh) aligns append along S — cheap. Head-major requires scatter per head when we append which is costly. So KV cache argues for seq-major.
alex: Good point. So maybe canonical layout: seq-major for KV cache (append-friendly), but when running Q/K/V compute we transform to head-major for fast per-head kernels if that's net-positive.
priya: We should quantify break-even: copy_cost + kernel_gain <= strided_kernel_perf. Add heuristics: if seq_len < 128 and batch==1 prefer copy+fused kernel; if seq_len>512 prefer strided streaming kernels.
sam: Also consider fused vs separate GEMMs: fused single GEMM to produce interleaved QKV reduces three GEMMs -> lower launch overhead. But if we then have to deinterleave for head-major layout, that is another cost. Keep both kernels and route by model config.
maria: Alignment and quantization notes: int8 kernels require per-row packing; layout choices change memory layout for scales/zeros which affects vectorized dequantize. Make sure our quantized kernel ABI includes stride and pad info.
devon: Action items: alex to draft kernel selector heuristics (copy vs strided vs fused) with thresholds. priya to add microbench harness for append-heavy KV cache patterns. sam to prototype a fused qkv -> head-major transform kernel that does in-place rearrange with minimal extra memory. I'll own perf traces for NV 40/80.
alex: Sounds good — I'll push a short RFC addendum with heuristics + a tiny table of expected costs. cc @maria @devon for quantization/kv notes. :thumbsup:
